speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you are here with acute diarrhea. To help me understand your situation, how many times have you had loose stools in the last 24 hours, and have there been any visible blood or pus in them?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a significant volume of diarrhea shortly after starting levofloxacin; have you experienced any fever, severe pain, or signs of dehydration such as dizziness? I need to check your stool for C. difficile toxins and request a stool culture to rule out other pathogens.

REQUEST TEST: C.diff toxin assay, Stool_Culture
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: C.diff toxin assay: Not specified; Stool_Culture: Pending; Abdominal_X-Ray: Not provided

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Watery diarrhea. I also have Lower abdominal discomfort, Abdominal cramping. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Levofloxacin-induced *Clostridioides difficile* infection. The timing of symptoms relative to antibiotic initiation, combined with watery diarrhea and lower abdominal pain, makes this the most likely cause, whereas a urinary tract infection typically presents with dysuria or frequency rather than significant diarrhea. Please ensure stool results are pending, as they will confirm this clinical suspicion.
